children: Japanese rubber futures eased on Monday as technical signals pointed to a possible correction after the contract's rally to multi-year highs, while a slide in Japanese equities on rising Bank of Japan rate-hike expectations also weighed on sentiment.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 2 yen, or 0.45%, at 440.6 yen ($2.76) per kg as of 0218 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 65 yuan, or 0.35%, to 18,875 yuan ($2,807.90) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 340 yuan, or 2.36%, to 14,730 yuan per metric ton.

The OSE contract is testing multi-year highs with the bullish trend likely intact, though prices are in overbought territory and point to a possible near-term correction before further gains, Japan Exchange Group said in a report on Monday.
share gauge fell nearly 2% on Monday on rising expectations for central bank rate hikes to tame inflation.
Rubber inventories in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange rose 0.5% week-on-week, the exchange said on Friday.

The global natural rubber market remains in deficit in 2026, though the key question for the second half is whether that tightens actual supply, given that purchasing has remained largely hand-to-mouth without a broad restocking cycle so far, the International Rubber Study Group said in a note.
Losses were limited, however, by a weakening currency, making yen-denominated assets more affordable to overseas buyers.
was slightly weaker at 160.01 per dollar, after sliding beyond the 160-per-dollar level on Friday, a level widely viewed as increasing the risk of official intervention.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 234.7 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.4%.
